title: Quran Study 65: Sura 2, Death, the Qiblah, Overwhelming Signs, and Idols (Composite, 1982-12)
date_note: The filename combines December 3 and December 10, 1982. The opening also continues themes and verses from Study 64, so exact internal dating requires the original tapes.
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/65 - Friday Sermon 03 Dec. 1982 & 10 Dec. 1982 By Dr Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: A composite file joining several connected discussions. The opening continues Quran 2:159–163 through concealed truth, repentance, death, angels, martyrs, the claim that believers die gently without pain, and the declaration that God is one. A lengthy geometric debate revisits the qiblah from Tucson through flat maps, globe surfaces, radii, straight lines, north and east, and the shortest route to Mecca. After an announcement about Arabic lessons, Rashad studies Quran 2:164 through human and animal design, teeth, swallowing, heartbeats, Earth, night and day, water, clouds, desert seeds, and wind. Quran 2:165–167 then describes idols disowning their followers. Jesus, Muhammad, Mary, Saint Jude, intercession, and Matthew 7:23 are used as examples.

related_duplicate_sources.note: The opening begins near Quran 2:159 after Study 64's Safa and Marwah block.
The qiblah block is secondary as an additional witness to the same debate.

content_guidance.instruction: Do not assign every block to a single day without verification.
It is an extended duplicate discussion.

content_guidance.rule: Separate scientific examples from Quranic text
content_guidance.instruction: Only the transcript is evidence of what was said.

sections.title: Concealed truth, repentance, death, angels, martyrs, painless belief, and Quran 2:163
sections.summary: The opening continues discussion of people who conceal or distort revelation and may repent by clarifying it. Rashad says disbelievers are beaten by angels at death, believers' souls are taken gently without pain, and martyrs experience an easy transition. Quran 2:163 is read in Arabic and English as the declaration that God is one, Gracious, and Merciful.
related_questions: What must a person who concealed truth do when repenting?
How were the deaths of believers and disbelievers contrasted?
sections.retrieval_note: Do not promise painless death or interpret a person's death as evidence of belief.

sections.title: Extended Tucson qiblah geometry: east, northeast, globe surfaces, radii, and straight lines
sections.summary: Participants spend roughly half an hour drawing and debating the direction from Tucson to Mecca. They compare map projections, compass bearings, a person's upright orientation on a sphere, radii from Earth's center, satellites, latitude and longitude, east, northeast, and what counts as a straight line or shortest route.
related_questions: Which geometric models were used in the qiblah debate?
Why did the participants disagree over east and northeast?
sections.retrieval_note: This overlaps Study 63 and is not reliable directional guidance.

sections.title: Quran 2:165–167, idols disown followers, Jesus, Muhammad, intercession, and Matthew 7:23
sections.summary: Quran 2:165–167 is read as a future event described in the past tense. Followers confront the people or figures they idolized, while those idols disown them. Rashad applies the verses to Jesus, Muhammad, Mary, Saint Jude, and intercession, and compares them with Matthew 7:23, where Jesus rejects people acting in his name.

sections.canonical_text: [2:167] The followers will then say, "If we could live our first life again, we will then disown them, as they disown us now." Thus, will GOD show them the consequences of their works as nothing but sorrow; they will never exit from Hell. Now,... These verses are actually written in the past tense in the Arabic. So, I guess in the next edition, I will, I will make these in the past tense. And they were in the past tense because God is telling us something that actually took place in our future. God witnessed it, and He's telling us what happened between the idols and the idol worshippers. And, and we saw today the insignificance of the idols, whether it is Muhammad or Jesus or Mary or Saint Francis or whatever, the things that the people idolize. The newspaper actually has prayers to Saint Jude for certain things. Today. Dr. Khalifa: I mean, in the newspapers in these days. A woman: (unintelligible) Dr. Khalifa: Huh? A woman: (unintelligible) Dr. Khalifa: Yeah. In the Personals. A woman: (unintelligible) Dr. Khalifa: Two days ago, this lady wrote to Ann Landers saying that she, she made a mistake investing her mother's life savings, and she was (unintelligible), she was praying to Mary and, and Saint Jude. And the title was The Virgin and Saint Jude will not help you. That was the title by Ann Landers. Now, so, we saw today the insignificance of the idols. We saw the picture of the earth and how, how big those people were, Muhammad or Mary or Jesus. Now, we have to imagine the Day of Judgment. Because that day will come. And the people will run to Jesus, for example, and tell him, "Are you gonna help us?" And he will say, "What are you talking about? I need help myself." Because he will be subject to the judgment, just we are, just like all of us. As a matter of fact, all of us will go, will see Hell first, initially, so that we appreciate Heaven, IN SHAA ALLAH, when we get there. But we must imagine that what these verses are telling us that the people will go to their idols. They will go to Muhammad. You heard about the myth of intercession of Muhammad. They will go, "will you intercede on our behalf?" And he's gonna tell them, "Sorry, I have no power. I'm worried about my own neck", Like Sura 21 tells us that the prophets will be worried about their own faith. This is what these verses are telling us. This is what the Bible is saying in Matthew 7:23, if you wanna see it, 7:23, Matthew 7:23 says, that the people will go to Jesus on the Day of Judgment and tell him, lord, lord, have we not prophesied in your name? Have we not performed miracles in your name? Have we not glorified your name? Etc, etc. And Jesus will say, Out of my sight, I don't know you. So, in other words, he will disown them. You just listen to the preachers on the TV and the radio of Sunday, and see how much glorification of Jesus they are doing. So, Satan succeeded in diverting their attention from God to Jesus. And Satan did the same trick with the Muslims, diverting their attention from God to Muhammad. They're all human beings and they're all subject to the, to Satan's tricks. So, these verses here are telling us that the idols will disown their worshippers. These verses are actually identical...
